extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and authors preparing submissions to the AAAI-25 Main Technical Track (prospective conference paper authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Call-for-papers and submission/review guidelines for authors submitting technical research papers to the AAAI-25 Main Technical Track. Covers topical scope, submission process, review criteria, formatting/supplementary-material rules, and ethics/policy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism & Use of ChatGPT or similar LLMs Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that include text generated from a large-scale language model (LLM) such as ChatGPT are prohibited unless the produced text is presented as a part of the paper’s experimental analysis. Any AI system does not satisfy the criteria for authorship and cannot be used as a citable source. Authors assume full responsibility for content, including checking for plagiarism and veracity of all text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may use LLMs for editing or polishing author-written text (allowed). Any allegation of plagiarism (including via LLM use) will be investigated and, if substantiated, may result in serious sanctions including rejection/retraction, notification to institutions, and denial of service/access to AAAI events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-phase reviewing process
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI uses a two-phase reviewing process: Phase 1 provides two reviews; papers not rejected in Phase 1 receive additional reviews in Phase 2. Author response is allowed after Phase 2 only for papers not rejected in Phase 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect initial triage and further review for borderline papers; behave accordingly (e.g., prepare strong submissions for Phase 1 and be ready to respond in Phase 2 if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material: allowed types and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Three kinds of supplementary material may be submitted alongside papers: (1) technical appendix; (2) multimedia; (3) code and data. Supplementary material deadline is 3 days after the paper submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare supplementary materials to support claims (proofs, additional experiments, multimedia demos, datasets, and code). Ensure timely upload within the 3-day window. Supplementary material can be used to facilitate reproducibility and reviewer evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional pages allowed for references only
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers may include additional pages beyond the page limit only for references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep main manuscript within page limits; place extra bibliography entries on allowed reference-only pages rather than in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility checklist requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must complete a reproducibility checklist, which facilitates replication of the reported research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the checklist accurately; provide sufficient methodological detail, data, and code where feasible to allow replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors expected to be available to review
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are expected to be available to review (light load), unless extenuating circumstances apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate availability and participate in peer review as part of community expectations; failure to be available may be noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical scope and encouragement of cross-cutting/bridge work
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-25 welcomes research that advances AI broadly, including machine learning, NLP, computer vision, data mining, multiagent systems, knowledge representation, human-in-the-loop AI, search, planning, reasoning, robotics, perception, and ethics. The conference expressly encourages work that cuts across technical areas of AI or bridges AI and related disciplines or application domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize interdisciplinary bridges, cross-area relevance, or application-driven AI when appropriate; consult AAAI-25 keywords and author guidance for selecting keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance and novelty of contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions will be evaluated and scored for the significance and novelty of the contributions (research problems or questions addressed, methods, experiments, analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the research problem, novelty relative to prior work, and why the contribution matters beyond a narrow incremental advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical and/or empirical soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will be evaluated for the theoretical and/or empirical soundness of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rigorous analysis, proofs, solid experimental design, appropriate baselines, statistical rigor, and clear interpretation of results so that claims are well-supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to the AAAI community
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the work is relevant to the AAAI community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame contributions in terms of interest and impact for AAAI attendees and researchers; situate work within AI research directions that matter to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will be evaluated for clarity of exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly and concisely, define terms, explain methods and experiments so reviewers can understand and reproduce the work; use figures/tables where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible research practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional considerations include adherence to responsible research practices (e.g., with respect to human subject studies, use of sensitive data, as well as data and algorithmic bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe ethical approvals, consent, data handling, fairness/bias mitigation, privacy protections, and any limitations or risks of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and sharing of artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation considers steps to ensure reproducibility of research results (e.g., by providing detailed proofs, documenting experiments, sharing data, and sharing code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include proofs/derivations in main paper or technical appendix, share code and data when possible, document experiment protocols, and provide seeds/configuration to enable replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for exploration/new territory over narrow incremental advances
rubrics_metrics.description: Solid, technical papers that explore new territory or point out new directions for research, or introduce new problems, address research questions, or introduce methods that are of interest beyond a single sub-area of AI are preferred to papers that advance the state of the art only incrementally, or only within a narrow sub-area of AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight broader interest, novelty, and potential to open new research directions rather than only marginal improvements on benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Track on AI for Social Impact (AISI) evaluation rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to the AI for Social Impact track will be reviewed according to a rubric that emphasizes the fit between the techniques used and a problem of social importance, rather than simply rewarding technical novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will assess: significance of the addressed problem; the paper's engagement with previous literature on the application problem (AI literature or domain-specific literature); novelty of and justification for the proposed AI-based approach; quality of evaluation; facilitation of follow-up work; and overall scope and promise for social impact. See the AISI page for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Track on AI Alignment evaluation note
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-25 includes a special track on AI Alignment; this track will be evaluated using criteria similar to but slightly different from the main track criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the AI Alignment (AIA) track CFP for specific review criteria; emphasize understanding risks of capable AI systems and methods to mitigate them, and tailor exposition to alignment concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeurIPS fast-track / simultaneous-submission policy note
rubrics_metrics.description: The NeurIPS fast track from previous years will not be included; the AAAI submission deadline is after NeurIPS initial reviews are released, and authors must withdraw the paper from consideration at NeurIPS if they wish to submit to AAAI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the same paper simultaneously to NeurIPS and AAAI; withdraw from NeurIPS if submitting to AAAI in this cycle.
